Then, you may throw yourself on the tomb, kiss it, and say these words: Ø¨ÙØ£ÙØ¨ÙÙ Ø£ÙÙÙØªÙ ÙÙØ£ÙÙ ÙÙÙ ÙÙØ§ Ø¨ÙÙÙ Ø±ÙØ³ÙÙÙÙ Ù±ÙÙÙÙÙÙ bi'abi anta wa ummi yabna rasuli allahi My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! Ø¨ÙØ£ÙØ¨ÙÙ Ø£ÙÙÙØªÙ ÙÙØ£ÙÙ ÙÙÙ ÙÙØ§ Ø£ÙØ¨ÙØ§ Ø¹ÙØ¨ÙØ¯Ù Ù±ÙÙÙÙÙÙ bi'abi anta wa ummi ya aba `abdillahi My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Abu `Abdullah! ÙÙÙÙØ¯Ù Ø¹ÙØ¸ÙÙ ÙØªÙ Ù±ÙØ±ÙÙØ²ÙÙÙÙØ©Ù laqad `azumat alrraziyyatu Extremely terrible was the calamity ÙÙØ¬ÙÙÙÙØªÙ Ù±ÙÙÙ ÙØµÙØ¨ÙØ©Ù Ø¨ÙÙÙ Ø¹ÙÙÙÙÙÙÙØ§ wa jallat almusibatu bika `alayna and astounding is the misfortune that you suffered upon us ÙÙØ¹ÙÙÙÙÙ° Ø¬ÙÙ ÙÙØ¹Ù Ø£ÙÙÙÙÙ Ù±ÙØ³ÙÙÙ ÙØ§ÙÙØ§ØªÙ ÙÙÙ±ÙØ£ÙØ±ÙØ¶Ù wa `ala jami`i ahli alssamawati wal-ardi and upon all the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. ÙÙÙÙØ¹ÙÙÙ Ù±ÙÙÙÙÙÙ Ø£ÙÙ ÙÙØ©Ù Ø£ÙØ³ÙØ±ÙØ¬ÙØªÙ ÙÙØ£ÙÙÙØ¬ÙÙ ÙØªÙ fala`ana allahu ummatan asrajat wa aljamat Therefore, Allah may curse the people who saddled up, gave rein to their horses, ÙÙØªÙÙÙÙÙÙØ£ÙØªÙ ÙÙÙÙØªÙØ§ÙÙÙÙ wa tahayya'at liqitalika and prepared themselves to kill you. ÙÙØ§ Ù ÙÙÙÙØ§ÙÙÙ ÙÙØ§ Ø£ÙØ¨ÙØ§ Ø¹ÙØ¨ÙØ¯Ù Ù±ÙÙÙÙÙÙ ya mawlaya ya aba `abdillahi O my Master, O Abu `Abdullah! ÙÙØµÙØ¯ÙØªÙ Ø­ÙØ±ÙÙ ÙÙÙ qasadtu haramaka I moved towards your sanctuary ÙÙØ£ÙØªÙÙÙØªÙ Ø¥ÙÙÙÙÙ° Ù ÙØ´ÙÙÙØ¯ÙÙÙ wa ataytu ila mashhadika and came to your shrine Ø£ÙØ³ÙØ£ÙÙÙ Ù±ÙÙÙÙÙÙ Ø¨ÙÙ±ÙØ´ÙÙØ£ÙÙÙ Ù±ÙÙÙØ°ÙÙ ÙÙÙÙ Ø¹ÙÙÙØ¯ÙÙÙ as'alu allaha bilshsha'ni alladhi laka `indahu beseeching Allah in the name of the standing that you enjoy with Him ÙÙØ¨ÙÙ±ÙÙÙ ÙØ­ÙÙÙÙ Ù±ÙÙÙØ°ÙÙ ÙÙÙÙ ÙÙØ¯ÙÙÙÙÙ wa bilmahalli alladhi laka ladayhi and the position that you occupy with Him Ø£ÙÙÙ ÙÙØµÙÙÙÙÙÙ Ø¹ÙÙÙÙÙ° Ù ÙØ­ÙÙ ÙÙØ¯Ù ÙÙØ¢ÙÙ Ù ÙØ­ÙÙ ÙÙØ¯Ù an yusalliya `ala muhammadin wa ali muhammadin to send ble

segments.arabic: بِسْمِ اللهِ الرّحْمٰنِ الرّحِیْمِ
segments.translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate

segments.arabic: اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ
segments.translation: Peace be upon you, O Abu-`Abdullah.

segments.arabic: اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا بْنَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ
segments.translation: Peace be upon you, O son of Allah’s Messenger.

segments.arabic: السَّلاَمُ عَلَيكَ يَا خِيَرَةِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱبْنَ خَيرَتِهِ
segments.transliteration: alssalamu `alayka ya khiyarata allahi wabna khiyaratihi
segments.translation: Peace be upon you, O choicest of Allah and son of His choicest.

segments.arabic: اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا بْنَ أَمِيرِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
segments.translation: Peace be upon you, O son of the Commander of the Faithful

segments.arabic: وَٱبْنَ سَيِّدِ ٱلْوَصِيِّينَ
segments.translation: and son of the chief of the Prophets’ successors.

segments.arabic: اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا بْنَ فَاطِمَةَ
segments.translation: Peace be upon you, O son of Fatimah

segments.arabic: سَيِّدَةِ نِسَاءِ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ
segments.translation: the doyenne of the women of the worlds.

segments.arabic: اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا ثَارَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱبْنَ ثَارِهِ وَٱلْوِتْرَ ٱلْمَوْتُورَ
segments.transliteration: alssalamu `alayka ya thara allahi wabna tharihi walwitra almawtura
segments.translation: Peace be upon you, O vengeance of Allah, son of His vengeance, and the unavenged so far.

segments.arabic: اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْوَاحِ ٱلَّتِي حَلَّتْ بِفِنَائِكَ
segments.transliteration: alssalamu `alayka wa `ala al-arwahi allati hallat bifina'ika
segments.translation: Peace be upon you and upon the souls that resided in your courtyard.

segments.arabic: عَلَيْكُمْ مِنِّي جَمِيعاً سَلاَمُ ٱللَّهِ أَبَداً
segments.translation: Peace of Allah be upon all of you from me forever

segments.arabic: مَا بَقيتُ وَبَقِيَ ٱللَّيْلُ وَٱلنَّهَارُ
segments.transliteration: ma baqitu wa baqiya allaylu walnnaharu
segments.translation: as long as I am existent and as long as there are day and night.

segments.arabic: يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ
segments.translation: O Abu-`Abdullah,

segments.arabic: لَقَدْ عَظُمَتِ ٱلرَّزِيَّةُ
segments.translation: unbearable is the sorrow

segments.arabic: وَجَلَّتْ وَعَظُمَتِ ٱلْمُصيبَةُ بِكَ
segments.translation: and excruciating and unbearable is the misfortune of you

segments.arabic: عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَىٰ جَمِيعِ أَهْلِ ٱلإِسْلاَمِ
segments.translation: for us and for all the people of Islam.

segments.arabic: وَجَلَّتْ وَعَظُمَتْ مُصيبَتُكَ
segments.translation: Excruciating and unbearable has been your misfortune

segments.arabic: فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ عَلَىٰ جَمِيعِ أَهْلِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ
segments.translation: in the heavens for all the inhabitants of the heavens.

segments.arabic: فَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ أُمَّةً أَسَّسَتْ أَسَاسَ ٱلظُّلْمِ وَٱلْجَوْرِ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ ٱلْبَيْتِ
segments.transliteration: fala`ana allahu ummatan assasat asasa alzzulmi waljawri `alaykum ahla albayti
segments.translation: So, may Allah curse the people who laid the basis of persecution and wronging against you, O Members of the Household.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ أُمَّةً دَفَعَتْكُمْ عَنْ مَقَامِكُمْ
segments.transliteration: wa la`ana allahu ummatan dafa`atkum `an maqamikum
segments.translation: May Allah curse the people who drove you away from your position

segments.arabic: وَأَزَالَتْكُمْ عَنْ مَرَاتِبِكُمُ ٱلَّتِي رَتَّبَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيهَا
segments.transliteration: wa azalatkum `an maratibikum allati rattabakum allahu fiha
segments.translation: and removed you away from your ranks that Allah has put you in.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ أُمَّةً قَتَلَتْكُمْ
segments.translation: May Allah curse the people who slew you.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُمَهِّدِينَ لَهُمْ
segments.translation: May Allah curse those who paved the way for them to do so

segments.arabic: بِٱلتَّمْكِينِ مِنْ قِتَالِكُمْ
segments.translation: and who made possible for them to fight against you.

segments.arabic: بَرِئْتُ إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ وَإِلَيْكُمْ مِنْهُمْ
segments.transliteration: bari'tu ila allahi wa ilaykum minhum
segments.translation: I repudiate them in the presence of Allah and You

segments.arabic: وَمِنْ أَشْيَاعِهِمْ وَأَتْبَاعِهِمْ وَأَوْلِيَائِهِمْ
segments.transliteration: wa min ashya`ihim wa atba`ihim wa awliya'ihim
segments.translation: and I repudiate their devotees, followers, and loyalists.

segments.arabic: يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ
segments.translation: O Abu-`Abdullah,

segments.arabic: إِنِّي سِلْمٌ لِمَنْ سَالَمَكُمْ
segments.translation: I am at peace with those who are at peace with you

segments.arabic: وَحَرْبٌ لِمَنْ حَارَبَكُمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ
segments.transliteration: wa harbun liman harabakum ila yawmi alqiyamati
segments.translation: and I am at war against those who have fought against you up to the Resurrection Day.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ آلَ زِيَادٍ وَآلَ مَرْوَانَ
segments.transliteration: wa la`ana allahu ala ziyadin wa ala marwana
segments.translation: May Allah also curse the family of Ziyad and the family of Marwan.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ قَاطِبَةً
segments.transliteration: wa la`ana allahu bani umayyata qatibatan
segments.translation: May Allah also curse the descendants of Umayyah altogether.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ ٱبْنَ مَرْجَانَةَ
segments.translation: May Allah also curse the son of Marjanah.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ عُمَرَ بْنَ سَعْدٍ
segments.translation: May Allah also curse `Umar the son of Sa`d.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ شِمْراً
segments.translation: May Allah also curse Shimr.

segments.arabic: وَلَعَنَ ٱللَّهُ أُمَّةً أَسْرَجَتْ وَأَلْجَمَتْ
segments.transliteration: wa la`ana allahu ummatan asrajat wa aljamat
segments.translation: May Allah also curse the people who saddled up, gave reins to their horses,

segments.arabic: وَتَنَقَّبَتْ لِقِتَالِكَ
segments.translation: and masked their faces in preparation for fighting against you.

segments.arabic: بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي
segments.translation: May my father and mother be ransoms for you.

segments.arabic: لَقَدْ عَظُمَ مُصَابِي بِكَ
segments.translation: Extremely insufferable is my commiserations with you;

segments.arabic: فَأَسْأَلُ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي أَكْرَمَ مَقَامَكَ وَأَكْرَمَنِي بِكَ
segments.transliteration: fa'as'alu allaha alladhi akrama maqamaka wa akramani bika
segments.translation: so, I beseech Allah Who has honored your position and honored me because of you

segments.arabic: أَنْ يَرْزُقَنِي طَلَبَ ثَأْرِكَ
segments.translation: to endue me with the chance to avenge you

segments.arabic: مَعَ إِمَامٍ مَنْصُورٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِ مُحَمَّدٍ
segments.transliteration: ma`a imamin mansurin min ahli bayti muhammadin
segments.translation: with a (Divinely) supported leader from the Household of Muhammad,

segments.arabic: صَلَّىٰ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ
segments.translation: peace of Allah be upon him and his Household.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱجْعَلْنِي عِنْدَكَ وَجِيهاً
segments.translation: O Allah, (please) make me illustrious in Your sight

segments.arabic: بِٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ
segments.translation: in the name of al-Husayn, peace be upon him, in this world and in the Hereafter.

segments.arabic: يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ
segments.translation: O Abu-`Abdullah,

segments.arabic: إِنِّي أَتَقَرَّبُ إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ وَإِلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ
segments.transliteration: inni ataqarrabu ila allahi wa ila rasulihi
segments.translation: I do seek nearness to Allah, to His Messenger,

segments.arabic: وَإِلَىٰ أَمِيرِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَإِلَىٰ فَاطِمَةَ
segments.transliteration: wa ila amiri almu'minina wa ila fatimata
segments.translation: to the Commander of the Faithful, to Fatimah,

segments.arabic: وَإِلَىٰ ٱلْحَسَنِ وَإِلَيْكَ بِمُوَالاَتِكَ
segments.transliteration: wa ila alhasani wa ilayka bimuwalatika
segments.translation: to al-Hasan, and to you by means of loyalty to you

segments.arabic: وَبِٱلْبَرَاءَةِ (مِمَّنْ قَاتَلَكَ
segments.translation: and by means of repudiation of those who fought against you

segments.arabic: وَنَصَبَ لَكَ ٱلْحَرْبَ
segments.translation: and incurred your hostility,

segments.arabic: وَبِٱلْبَرَاءَةِ مِمَّنْ أَسَّسَ أَسَاسَ ٱلظُّلْمِ وَٱلْجَوْرِ عَلَيْكُمْ
segments.transliteration: wa bilbara'ati mimman assasa asasa alzzulmi waljawri `alaykum
segments.translation: and repudiation of those who laid the basis of persecution and wronging against you all.

segments.arabic: وَأَبْرَأُ إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ وَإِلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ)
segments.transliteration: wa abra'u ila allahi wa ila rasulihi)
segments.translation: I also repudiate, in the presence of Allah and His Messenger,

segments.arabic: مِمَّنْ أَسَّسَ أَسَاسَ ذٰلِكَ
segments.translation: those who laid the basis of all that,

segments.arabic: وَبَنَىٰ عَلَيْهِ بُنْيَانَهُ
segments.translation: established their foundations on it,

segments.arabic: وَجَرَىٰ فِي ظُلْمِهِ وَجَوْرِهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعلىٰ أَشْيَاعِكُمْ
segments.transliteration: wa jara fi zulmihi wa jawrihi `alaykum wa `ala ashya`ikum
segments.translation: and continued in wronging and persecuting you and your adherents.

segments.arabic: بَرِئْتُ إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ وَإِلَيْكُمْ مِنْهُمْ
segments.transliteration: bari'tu ila allahi wa ilaykum minhum
segments.translation: In the presence of Allah and you all do I repudiate these.

segments.arabic: وَأَتَقَرَّبُ إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْكُمْ
segments.transliteration: wa ataqarrabu ila allahi thumma ilaykum
segments.translation: And I seek nearness to Allah and then to you all

segments.arabic: بِمُوَالاَتِكُمْ وَمُوَالاَةِ وَلِيِّكُمْ
segments.translation: by means of declaring loyalty to you and to your loyalists

segments.arabic: وَبِٱلْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْ أَعْدَائِكُمْ
segments.translation: and declaring repudiation of your enemies

segments.arabic: وَٱلنَّاصِبِينَ لَكُمُ ٱلْحَرْبَ
segments.translation: and those who incur animosity of you

segments.arabic: وَبِٱلْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْ أَشْيَاعِهِمْ وَأَتْبَاعِهِمْ
segments.transliteration: wa bilbara'ati min ashya`ihim wa atba`ihim
segments.translation: and repudiation of their adherents and followers.

segments.arabic: إِنِّي سِلْمٌ لِمَنْ سَالَمَكُمْ
segments.translation: I am verily at peace with those who have been at peace with you,

segments.arabic: وَحَرْبٌ لِمَنْ حَارَبَكُمْ
segments.translation: I am at war against those who fought against you,

segments.arabic: وَوَلِيٌّ لِمَنْ وَالاَكُمْ
segments.translation: loyalist to those who have been loyalist to you,

segments.arabic: وَعَدُوٌّ لِمَنْ عَادَاكُمْ
segments.translation: and enemy of those who have shown enmity towards you.

segments.arabic: فَأَسْأَلُ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي أَكْرَمَنِي بِمَعْرِفَتِكُمْ
segments.translation: So, I beseech Allah Who has endued me with the honor of recognizing you

segments.arabic: وَمَعْرِفَةِ أَوْلِيَائِكُمْ
segments.translation: and recognizing your loyalists

segments.arabic: وَرَزَقَنِيَ ٱلْبَرَاءَةَ مِنْ أَعْدَائِكُمْ
segments.translation: and Who conferred upon me with repudiation of your enemies,

segments.arabic: أَنْ يَجْعَلَنِي مَعَكُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ
segments.transliteration: an yaj`alani ma`akum fi alddunya wal-akhirati
segments.translation: to include me with you in this world and in the Hereafter

segments.arabic: وَأَنْ يُثَبِّتَ لِي عِنْدَكُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ
segments.transliteration: wa an yuthabbita li `indakum qadama sidqin
segments.translation: and to make firm step of honesty for me with you

segments.arabic: فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ
segments.translation: in this world and in the Hereafter.

segments.arabic: وَأَسْأَلُهُ أَنْ يُبَلِّغَنِيَ ٱلْمَقَامَ ٱلْمَحْمُودَ لَكُمْ عِنْدَ ٱللَّهِ
segments.transliteration: wa as'aluhu an yuballighani almaqama almahmuda lakum `inda allahi
segments.translation: I also beseech Him to make me attain the praiseworthy status that you enjoy with Allah

segments.arabic: وَأَنْ يَرْزُقَنِي طَلَبَ ثَأْرِي
segments.translation: and to bestow upon me with the chance to take my own vengeance

segments.arabic: مَعَ إِمَامِ هُدىًٰ ظَاهِرٍ
segments.translation: with a leader of true guidance who is (Divinely) sustained

segments.arabic: نَاطِقٍ بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْكُمْ
segments.translation: and expressing the truth from among you.

segments.arabic: وَأَسْأَلُ ٱللَّهَ بِحَقِّكُمْ
segments.translation: I also beseech Allah in your names

segments.arabic: وَبِٱلشَّأْنِ ٱلَّذِي لَكُمْ عِنْدَهُ
segments.translation: and in the name of the standing that you enjoy with Him

segments.arabic: أَنْ يُعْطِيَنِي بِمُصَابِي بِكُمْ
segments.translation: to recompense me for my commiserations for you

segments.arabic: أَفْضَلَ مَا يُعْطِي مُصَاباً بِمُصِيبَتِهِ
segments.translation: with the most favorite thing that He ever gives as compensation for misfortunes that has afflicted anyone.

segments.arabic: مُصِيبَةً مَا أَعْظَمَهَا
segments.translation: (Your) misfortune has been so astounding

segments.arabic: وَأَعْظَمَ رَزِيَّتَهَا فِي ٱلإِسْلاَمِ
segments.translation: and so catastrophic for Islam

segments.arabic: وَفِي جَمِيعِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ
segments.translation: and for all the heavens and the entire earth.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱجْعَلْنِي فِي مَقَامِي هٰذَا
segments.translation: O Allah, (please) make me in this situation of mine

segments.arabic: مِمَّنْ تَنَالُهُ مِنْكَ صَلَوَاتٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ
segments.transliteration: mimman tanaluhu minka salawatun wa rahmatun wa maghfiratun
segments.translation: one of those who receive blessings, mercy, and forgiveness from You.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ مَحْيَايَ مَحْيَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
segments.transliteration: allahumma ij`al mahyaya mahya muhammadin wa ali muhammadin
segments.translation: O Allah, (please) make me live my lifetime in the same way as Muhammad and Muhammad’s Household lived

segments.arabic: وَمَمَاتِي مَمَاتَ مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
segments.transliteration: wa mamati mamata muhammadin wa ali muhammadin
segments.translation: and make me die on the same principles on which Muhammad and Muhammad’s Household died.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّ هٰذَا يَوْمٌ
segments.translation: O Allah, this day

segments.arabic: تَبَرَّكَتْ بِهِ بَنُو أُمَيَّةَ
segments.translation: has been regarded as blessed day by the descendants of Umayyah

segments.arabic: وَٱبْنُ آكِلَةِ ٱلأَكبَادِ
segments.translation: and by the son of the liver-eater woman,

segments.arabic: ٱللَّعِينُ ٱبْنُ ٱللَّعِينِ
segments.translation: the accursed and son of the accursed

segments.arabic: عَلَىٰ لِسَانِكَ وَلِسَانِ نَبِيِّكَ
segments.translation: by the tongue of You and by the tongue of Your Prophet,

segments.arabic: صَلَّىٰ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ
segments.translation: Allah’s peace be upon him,

segments.arabic: فِي كُلِّ مَوْطِنٍ وَمَوْقِفٍ
segments.translation: on every occasion and in every situation,

segments.arabic: وَقَفَ فِيهِ نَبِيُّكَ صَلَّىٰ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ
segments.transliteration: waqafa fihi nabiyyuka salla allahu `alayhi wa alihi
segments.translation: which Your Prophet, Allah’s peace be upon him, attended.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱلْعَنْ أَبَا سُفْيَانَ وَمُعَاوِيَةَ وَيَزيدَ بْنَ مُعَاوِيَةَ
segments.transliteration: allahumma il`an aba sufyana wa mu`awiyata wa yazida bna mu`awiyata
segments.translation: O Allah, pour curses upon Abu-Sufyan, Mu`awiyah, and Yazid son of Mu`awiyah.

segments.arabic: عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْكَ ٱللَّعْنَةُ أَبَدَ ٱلآبِدِينَ
segments.translation: May Your curse be upon them incessantly and everlastingly.

segments.arabic: وَهٰذَا يَوْمٌ فَرِحَتْ بِهِ آلُ زِيَادٍ وَآلُ مَرْوَانَ
segments.transliteration: wa hadha yawmun farihat bihi alu ziyadin wa alu marwana
segments.translation: This is the day on which the family of Ziyad and the family of Marwan gloated

segments.arabic: بِقَتْلِهِمُ ٱلْحُسَيْنَ صَلَوَاتُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
segments.translation: because they had killed al-Husayn, Allah’s blessings be upon him.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ فَضَاعِفْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱللَّعْنَ مِنْكَ
segments.translation: So, O Allah, pour frequent curses upon them

segments.arabic: وَٱلْعَذَابَ (ٱلأَلِيمَ)
segments.translation: and double for them the painful chastisement.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَتَقَرَّبُ إِلَيْكَ فِي هٰذَا ٱلْيَوْمِ
segments.transliteration: allahumma inni ataqarrabu ilayka fi hadha alyawmi
segments.translation: O Allah, I do seek nearness to You on this day,

segments.arabic: وَفِي مَوْقِفِي هٰذَا
segments.translation: on this occasion,

segments.arabic: وَأَيَّامِ حَيَاتِي
segments.translation: and on all the days of my lifetime,

segments.arabic: بِٱلْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْهُمْ وَٱللَّعْنَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ
segments.translation: by repudiating these and invoking Your curses upon them,

segments.arabic: وَبِٱلْمُوَالاَةِ لِنَبِيِّكَ وَآلِ نَبِيِّكَ
segments.transliteration: wa bilmuwalati linabiyyika wa ali nabiyyika
segments.translation: and by declaring loyalty to Your Prophet and Your Prophet’s Household,

segments.arabic: عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
segments.translation: peace be upon him and them.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱلْعَنْ أَوَّلَ ظَالِمٍ
segments.translation: O Allah, pour curses upon the foremost persecutor

segments.arabic: ظَلَمَ حَقَّ مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
segments.transliteration: zalama haqqa muhammadin wa ali muhammadin
segments.translation: who usurped the right of Muhammad and Muhammad’s Household

segments.arabic: وَآخِرَ تَابِعٍ لَهُ عَلَىٰ ذٰلِكَ
segments.translation: and the last follower who acceded to his deed.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱلْعَنِ ٱلْعِصَابَةَ ٱلَّتِي جَاهَدَتِ ٱلْحُسَيْنَ
segments.transliteration: allahumma il`an al`isabata allati jahadat alhusayna
segments.translation: O Allah, pour curses upon the gang that struggled against al-Husayn

segments.arabic: وَشَايَعَتْ وَبَايَعَتْ وَتَابَعَتْ عَلَىٰ قَتْلِهِ
segments.transliteration: wa shaya`at wa baya`at wa taba`at `ala qatlihi
segments.translation: and who supported each other against him, paid homage to his enemies, and participated in slaying him.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱلْعَنْهُمْ جَمِيعاً
segments.translation: O Allah, pour curses upon all of them.

segments.arabic: اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ
segments.translation: Peace be upon you, O Abu-`Abdullah

segments.arabic: وَعَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْوَاحِ ٱلَّتِي حَلَّتْ بِفِنَائِكَ
segments.translation: and upon the souls that gathered in your courtyard.

segments.arabic: عَلَيْكَ مِنِّي سَلاَمُ ٱللَّهِ أَبَداً
segments.translation: Peace of Allah be upon you from me forever

segments.arabic: مَا بَقيتُ وَبَقِيَ ٱللَّيْلُ وَٱلنَّهَارُ
segments.transliteration: ma baqitu wa baqiya allaylu walnnaharu
segments.translation: as long as I am existent and as long as there are day and night.

segments.arabic: وَلاَ جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ آخِرَ ٱلْعَهْدِ مِنِّي لِزِيَارَتِكُمْ
segments.transliteration: wa la ja`alahu allahu akhira al`ahdi minni liziyaratikum
segments.translation: May Allah not cause this (visit) to be the last of my visit to you (all).

segments.arabic: اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَىٰ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ
segments.translation: Peace be upon al-Husayn,

segments.arabic: وَعَلَىٰ عَلِيِّ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ
segments.translation: upon `Ali ibn al-Husayn,

segments.arabic: وَعَلَىٰ أَوْلاَدِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ
segments.translation: upon the sons of al-Husayn,

segments.arabic: وَعَلَىٰ أَصْحَابِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ
segments.translation: and upon the companions of al-Husayn.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ خُصَّ أَنْتَ أَوَّلَ ظَالِمٍ بِٱللَّعْنِ مِنِّي
segments.transliteration: allahumma khussa anta awwala zalimin billa`ni minni
segments.translation: O Allah, pour special curses on the foremost persecutor

segments.arabic: وَٱبْدَأْ بِهِ أَوَّلًا
segments.translation: and begin with him first,

segments.arabic: ثُمَّ ٱلْعَنِ ٱلثَّانِيَ وَٱلثَّالِثَ وَٱلرَّابِعَ
segments.translation: and then pour curses on the second, the third, and the fourth.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱلْعَنْ يَزِيدَ خَامِساً
segments.translation: O Allah, curse Yazid fifthly,

segments.arabic: وَٱلْعَنْ عُبَيْدَ ٱللَّهِ بْنَ زِيَادٍ وَٱبْنَ مَرْجَانَةَ
segments.translation: and curse `Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, the son of Marjanah,

segments.arabic: وَعُمَرَ بْنَ سَعْدٍ وَشِمْراً
segments.translation: `Umar ibn Sa`d, Shimr,

segments.arabic: وَآلَ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ وَآلَ زِيَادٍ وَآلَ مَرْوَانَ
segments.transliteration: wa ala abi sufyana wa ala ziyadin wa ala marwana
segments.translation: the family of Abu-Sufyan, the family of Ziyad, and the family of Marwan

segments.arabic: إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ
segments.translation: up to the Resurrection Day.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ لَكَ ٱلْحَمْدُ
segments.translation: O Allah, all praise be to You;

segments.arabic: حَمْدَ ٱلشَّاكِرِينَ لَكَ عَلَىٰ مُصَابِهِمْ
segments.translation: the praise of those who thank You for their misfortunes.

segments.arabic: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَىٰ عَظِيمِ رَزِيَّتِي
segments.translation: All praise be to Allah for my great misfortune.

segments.arabic: اَللَّهُمَّ ٱرْزُقْنِي شَفَاعَةَ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ يَوْمَ ٱلْوُرُودِ
segments.transliteration: allahumma irzuqni shafa`ata alhusayni yawma alwurudi
segments.translation: O Allah, (please) grant me the intercession of al-Husayn on the Day of Coming (to You)

segments.arabic: وَثَبِّتْ لِي قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَكَ
segments.translation: and make for me with You a firm step of honesty

segments.arabic: مَعَ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ وَأَصْحَابِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ
segments.translation: with al-Husayn and the companions of al-Husayn

segments.arabic: ٱلَّذينَ بَذَلُوٱ مُهَجَهُمْ دُونَ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
segments.translation: who sacrificed their souls in defense of al-Husayn, peace be upon him.

text: Ziyarah Nahiya Salutation on Imam Hussain(as) by Imam Mahdi(ajtfs) Signifance of this ziyarah Signifance of this ziyarah × Introduction and Translation by: Vahid Majd Naba Organization ISBN: 964-8323-13-5, First Edition: 2004Email: [email protected] âBut as I have been hindered by the course of time, and (Allahâs) decree has prevented me from helping you, and as I could not fight those who fought you, and was not able to show hostility to those who showed hostility to you, I will, therefore, lament you morning and evening, and will weep blood in place of tears, out of my anguish for you and my sorrow for all that befell youâ¦â âImam al-Mahdi (PBUH) Of the several prescribed Ziyarat of Imam al-Husain (PBUH), one was recited by Imam al-Mahdi (PBUH) and reached us through one of his four special deputies. For that reason, it is known as the Ziyarat that was issued from the sacred side (Ziyarat al-Nahiya al-Muqaddasa).[1] One of the most important features of this Ziyarat is that in different phrases, Imam al-Mahdi (PBUH) graphically describes the events of Ashura and the agony that Imam al-Husain (PBUH) and his family faced on that horrific and ominous day. The text of the Ziyarat al-Nahiya is found in some early Ziyarat collections such as al-Mazar al-Kabir, by Muhammad Ibn Jaâfar al-Mashâhadi, pp. 496-513. It is also reported in al-Mazar, by al-Mufid as mentioned in Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 98, pp. 318-329. An overview of the Ziyarat al-Nahiya Since this Ziyarat (as reported in al-Mazar al-Kabir, by al-Mashâhadi) originated from an infallible Imam who is the tongue of Allah, it is replete with divine recognition, guidance, spirituality, knowledge of religion, lessons for humanity, and the historical facts. The method of presentation in this Ziyarat follows the formal method seen in other texts by Ahl al-Bait (PBUT). The text of this Ziyarat can be divided into the following ten major parts: 1- Offering peace and salutations to the Prophets (PBUT) (whose spiritual heir was Imam al-Husain (PBUH)), from the earliest ones up to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH&HF), and then his pure progeny (PBUT) in addition to describing some of their attributes. For instance, we recite: âPeace be upon Adam, the chosen one of Allah from among His creation ...â 2- Offering peace and salutations to the Chief of Martyrs (PBUH) and enumerating some of his spiritual qualities and divine titles: âPeace be upon al-Husain who sacrificed himself up to the last drops of the blood of his heart. Peace be upon him, who obeyed Allah secretly and openly... Peace be upon the son of the Garden of refuge. Peace be upon the son of Zamzam and al-Safaa. Peace be upon him who was saturated in (his) blood ...â 3- Sending salutations to the martyrs of Karbala, in general, who sacrificed their selves for the divine cause: âPeace be upon the bloodstained chests... Peace be upon the pallid bodies... Peace be upon the dismembered limbs. Peace be upon the heads raised upon lances ...â 4- Stating the motivations, wishes, and aims for visiting Imam al-Husain (PBUH): âPeace be upon you! Indeed, I intended your visitation and am hopeful of achieving the prosperity that is with you. Salutations to you, salutations from he who recognizes your sanctity, is a sincere (believer) in your guardianship, seeks nearness to Allah through your love, and is aloof from your enemies ...â 5- Bearing witness to the Imamâs exemplary way of conduct: âI bear witness that you certainly established prayer, gave alms, enjoined good, forbade evil and transgression, obeyed Allah, never disobeyed Him, held fast to Him and to His rope, pleased Him, and held Him in awe ...â 6- Explaining the Imamâs method of opposing evil: âwhen tyranny became wide-spread, injustice removed its veil, wickedness called upon its followers... the knowledge demanded you for disavowal (of falsehood), and made it incumbent on you to struggle against the deviant. Therefore, you set out in company of your children, kinsfolk, followers, and supporters, disclosed the truth and clear proofs, summoned people towards Allah with wisdom and fine exhortation ...â 7- Presenting some of the calamities and afflictions that befell the Imam, and describing his martyrdom and the capture of his family: âThe enemy then surrounded you from all sides, weakened you by inflicting wounds, while you did not have any helper left, and you were bereaved yet patient ...â 8- Enumerating the depth of the crime: âCertainly, by killing you, they have killed Islam, disrupted (the truth of) prayer and fasting, revoked the (prophetic) customs and the (divine) laws... Certainly, (by this event,) the Messenger of Allah (PBUH&HF) was wronged, left alone, and denied vengeance, the Book of Allah, the mighty and the majestic, was again abandoned ...â 9- Relating the mourning ceremonies of the Prophets, Angels, and the cosmos: âIndeed, the Messenger (PBUH&HF) became distressed and his depressed heart wept. The Angels and the Prophets offered their condolences to him for your martyrdom. Your mother, al-Zahra, became distressed and bereft of you. Legions of Angels came in waves to offer their condolences to your father, the Leader of the Faithful ...â 10- Praying to Allah and imploring Him: âO Allah! By the sanctity of this exalted place (the tomb of Imam al-Husain (PBUH)), bestow blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, assemble me in their company, and admit me to Paradise by their intercession ...â A blend of wisdom, cognizance, spirituality, ethics, elegy, enthusiasm, devotion, along with a detailed account of the events has made this divinely inspired Ziyarat, one of the most insightful Ziyarat of Imam al-Husain (PBUH) for the followers of Ahl al-Bait (PBUT). In what follows, the Arabic text alongside its English translation and transliteration of the original Ziyarat al-Nahiya as reported in al-Mazar al-Kabir, by Muhammad Ibn al-Mashâhadi, is presented. May Allah hasten the advent of Imam Mahdi (PBUH), the reviver of the religion of Allah, the avenger of the blood of the Chief of Martyrs (PBUH) from the oppressors, and the establisher of peace and justice over the globe. With request for prayers, Vahid J. Majd, 1 Dhul-Hijja 1424. Imam Mahdi (PBUH) said, âI pray for any believer who remembers the sufferings of my martyred grandfather, al-Husain (PBUH), and then prays for my relief (al-Faraj)â Mikyal al-Makarim fi Fawaâidi Dâuaa lil Qaâim, by Sayyid Muhammad Taqi Musawi al-Isfahani, vol. 2, p.75. Documentation of the Ziyarat The text of the Ziyarat al-Nahiya is found in some early Ziyarat collections such as al-Mazar al-Kabir, by Muhammad Ibn Jaâfar al-Mashâhadi, pp. 496-513. It is also reported in al-Mazar, by al-Mufid as mentioned in Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 98, pp. 318-329. It is noteworthy that Sayyid Ibn Tawus (d. 664 AH) in his Misbah al-Zaâir reports another Ziyarat, which has some common parts with Ziyarat al-Nahiya. However, this Ziyarat has not been attributed to the Imam (PBUH), and has been only ascribed to Sayyid Murtadha (d. 436 AH). As al-Majlisi mentioned in Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 98, p. 251, although these variations might have been due to different narrations, yet this Ziyarat is apparently the composition of Sayyid Murtadha (RA) who used a part of original Ziyarat al-Nahiya, made some changes to it, added some phrases from other Ziyarats, and used to recite it as his own Ziyarat. It should be noted that there is another Ziyarat known as al-Nahiya, which focuses on the Ziyarat of other martyrs of Karbala, specifying the names of the companions of Imam al-Husain (PBUH). However, as mentioned by al-Majlisi, the time mentioned in the documentation of the Hadith as the time of its release is four years before the time of the birth of Imam al-Mahdi (PBUH). Assuming that it was not a transcription error, that particular Ziyarat may have been transmitted by Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH) (Imam Mahdiâs father, the eleventh Imam), not Imam Mahdi (PBUH). In that case, al-Nahiya al-Muqaddasa (the sacred place) refers to the house of Imam Hasan al-Askari (PBUH) in Samarra. × . For that reason, it is known as al-Muqaddasa. One of the most important features of this Ziyarat is that in different phrases, Imam al-Mahdi (as) graphically describes the events of Ashura and the agony that Imam al-Husain (as) and his family faced on that horrific and ominous day. Although the majority of these prayers are not dedicated to Fridays, it is highly recommended to offer them on Fridays. We plead to Allah to complete His rewards for them, grant them an increase, and recompense us pleasingly; He is the most Merciful, the most Compassionate. Allah suffices us, and He is the best Guardian.

segments.translation: Peace be upon Adam, the chosen one of Allah,
Peace be upon Noah, the Prophet of Allah,
Peace be upon Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah,
Peace be upon Moses, the one who spoke with Allah,
Peace be upon Jesus, the spirit of Allah,
Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah,
Peace be upon you, O best of Allahâs creation,
Peace be upon you, O chosen one of Allah,
Peace be upon you, O Muhammad son of Abdullah, the seal of the Prophets,
Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, the successor of the Messenger of Allah,
Peace be upon you, O Fatimah, the leader of the women of the worlds,
Peace be upon you both, O grandsons of the Prophet of Mercy,
And leaders of the youth of Paradise,
Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Husayn, the leader of the worshipers and the delight of those who behold,
Peace be upon you, O Muhammad ibn Ali, the expounder of knowledge after the Prophet,
Peace be upon you, O Ja'far ibn Muhammad, the truthful, the righteous, and the trustworthy,
Peace be upon you, O Musa ibn Ja'far, the pure and virtuous,
Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha, the chosen one,
Peace be upon you, O Muhammad ibn Ali, the pious,
Peace be upon you, O Ali ibn Muhammad, the pure, the sincere, and the trustworthy,
Peace be upon you, O Hasan ibn Ali,
Peace be upon the guardian after him,
O Allah, send blessings upon Your light, Your lamp, and the protector of Your protector,
The successor of Your successor and Your proof over Your creation,
Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah,
Peace be upon you, O daughter of Fatimah and Khadijah,
Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Commander of the Faithful,
Peace be upon you, O sister of Hasan and Husayn,
Peace be upon you, O daughter of the guardian of Allah,
Peace be upon you, O sister of the guardian of Allah,
Peace be upon you, O aunt of the guardian of Allah, and the mercy and blessings of Allah,
Peace be upon you; may Allah unite us and you in Paradise,
And may He gather us in your group,
And may He lead us to the fountain of your Prophet,
And may He quench our thirst with the cup of your grandfather, from the hand of Ali ibn Abi Talib,
Blessings of Allah be upon you,
I ask Allah to show us joy and relief through you,
And to gather us and you in the group of your grandfather Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family,
And that He does not deprive us of knowing you,
Indeed, He is a guardian and powerful,
I seek closeness to Allah through my love for you,
And my disassociation from your enemies,
And submission to Allah, content with Him, neither denying nor being arrogant,
And with certainty in what Muhammad brought,
And being pleased with it, we seek thereby Your countenance, O my Master,
O Allah, and Your pleasure and the Hereafter,
O my lady, O Zaynab,
Intercede for me in Paradise,
For you have a significant status before Allah,
O Allah, I ask You to conclude my life with happiness,
And do not take away from me what I am in,
And there is no power or strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Great,
O Allah, accept this from us through Your generosity and might,
And through Your mercy and well-being,
And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and all his family,
And peace and salutations be upon them, O the most merciful of the merciful.

text: Lady Zainab binte Ali Ibn Abutalib(as) ( peace be upon her) Brief info Brief Life × Zaynab is thought to mean 'she who weeps excessively', and other linguistic sources state that it once meant a good looking or smelling tree. The name might also possibly be a compound of the two Arabic words, zayn (beauty) and ab (father). Birth on 5th Jamadi Awal 5 AH (1st shaban also recorded ) Death -15th Rajab 62 AH (Other dates also recorded in Jamadi uth-thani, the 24th of Safar, or the 16th of Dhu'l-Hijjah) Zaynab is thought to mean 'she who weeps excessively', and other linguistic sources state that it once meant a good looking or smelling tree. The name might also possibly be a compound of the two Arabic words, zayn (beauty) and ab (father). Birth on 5th Jamadi Awal 5 AH (1st shaban also recorded ) Death -15th Rajab (Image) (Other dates also recorded in Jamadi uth-thani, the 24th of Safar, or the 16th of Dhu'l-Hijjah) Sayyeda Zainab (s.a.), the daughter of Imam Ali (a.s.) and Sayyeda Fatima (s.a.), was an exemplary woman of great ability, intelligence, knowledge, insight, courage and perseverance; she performed her divine duties to the best of her ability. She was born to a family formed by the Prophet (SAW), the most outstanding figure in history. The Prophet's wife Sayyeda Khadija (s.a.) a devoted woman, was her maternal grandmother, and her paternal grandmother was Fatima daughter of Assad, who mothered and nursed the Prophet (SAW). The members of the family, in trio hierarchical order, were all great. Sayyeda Zainab (s.a.) was a brilliant star in the mandate sky that received rays of holiness from the five suns. It was through her holy origins and pious edification that she manifested so great a fortitude in Karbala (Iraq). The life of the daughter of Sayyeda Al-Zahra (s.a.) was always laden with hardships, but she never feared coping with difficulties, this enhanced her endurance and elevated her soul. Extract From 'Victory of Truth' Book.... It was five years after the Muslims had accompanied the Prophet [s.a.w.] and his family in the migration (hijrah) to Medina, when the Holy Prophet's daughter, Hadrat Fatima [a.s.], gave birth to a little girl. When her father, Imam Ali [a.s.], saw his daughter for the first time Imam Husayn [a.s.], who was then almost three years old, was with him. The boy exclaimed in delight, "O father, Allah has given me a sister." At those words Imam Ali [a.s.] began to weep, and when Husayn [a.s.] asked why he was crying so, his father answered that he would soon come to know. Fatima [a.s.] and Ali [a.s.] did not name their child until a few days after her birth, for they awaited the Prophet's return from a journey so that he could propose the name. When finally the baby girl was brought before him he held her in his lap and kissed her. The Angel Jibra'il came to him and conveyed the name that was to be hers, and then he began to weep. The Prophet [s.a.w.] asked why Jibra'il wept and he answered, "O Prophet of Allah, from early on in life this girl will remain entangled in tribulations and trials in this world.- First she will weep over your separation (from this world); thereafter she will bemoan the loss of her mother, then her father, and then her brother Hasan. After all this she will be confronted with the trials of the land of Karbala and the tribulations of that lonely desert, as a result of which her hair will turn grey and her back will be bent." When the members of the family heard this prophecy they all broke down in tears. Imam Husayn [a.s.] now understood why earlier his father had also wept. Then the Prophet [s.a.w.] named her Zaynab [a.s.]. When the news of Zaynab's birth reached Salman al-Farsi, he went to Ali [a.s.] to congratulate him. But instead of seeing him happy and rejoicing he saw Ali [a.s.] shed tears, and he too was apprised of the events of Karbala and the hardships that were to befall Zaynab [a.s.]. One day, when Zaynab [a.s.] was about five years old, she had a strange and terrible dream. A violent wind arose in the city and darkened the earth and the sky. The little girl was tossed hither and thither, and suddenly she found herself stuck in the branches of a huge tree. But the wind was so strong that it uprooted the tree. Zaynab [a.s.] caught hold of a branch but that broke. In a panic she grabbed two twigs but these too gave way and she was left falling with no support. Then she woke up. When she told her grandfather, the Prophet [s.a.w.], about this dream he wept bitterly and said, "O my daughter that tree is me who is shortly going to leave this world. The branches are your father Ali and your mother Fatima Zahra, and the twigs are your brothers Hasan and Husayn. They will all depart this world before you do, and you will suffer their separation and loss." The exact date of her birth is uncertain; however the most widely accepted dates are the first of Sha'ban or the fifth of Jamadi ul-Awwal of the fifth or sixth year A.H., or the ninth of Ramadan in the ninth year A.H. p.45-6 ibid. p.68 ibid. The date of her death is uncertain : she is variously thought to be buried (most popularly) in Damascus, There are two explanations given as to how she came to be buried in Damascus: one being that some time after their return Yazid once again sent his forces to attack them, this time at Medina, and she and other members of her family were taken as prisoners of war to Damascus where she died; another being that because of a famine that swept through Medina, her husband temporarily moved his family to a village near Damascus, and it was there while praying in a garden that Zaynab [a.s.] was accidentally but fatally struck by a gardener's spade, or fell victim to a serious illness from which she never recovered. The anniversary of her death is observed on the following dates: 15th rajab ,11th or 21st of Jamadi uth-thani, the 24th of Safar, or the 16th of Dh u'l-Hijjah. Death Anniversary on 15th Rajab The death of the vanguard of protection for the members of the family of the Prophet and the lady who carried forth the message of Kerbala for the future generations, Lady Zainab the daughter of Ali (AS) holds a special place in the hearts of all Muslims. Born into a family of spiritual purity with a grand-father, mother, father, and brothers belonging to the tree of infallibility and the house in which the Qurâan descended, her environment was one which permitted her to reach to great levels. Although she lost her mother when she was still a child of around 7 years, another Fatimah (later on she became known as Ummul Baneen), entered into her fatherâs life and took on the arduous task of raising future leaders of the Ummah. However, the loss of her mother at such a young age did not prevent her from picking up her exemplary qualities. Just as her mother stood up to speak in the Masjid of the Prophet when her rights were stolen from her (in regards to Fadak), so too when the caravan of the Ahlul Bayt were taken to the palaces of Ibne Ziyad and Yazid, this daughter of Fatimah, as the mirror image of her mother, stood up to defend the Ahlul Bait and their rights. A model woman for all generations, one of her claims to fame was her profound knowledge of Islam. Although she never frequented a school to learn the faith of Islam, memorization of the Qurâan and the commentary of the Book of Allah (swt) and all other aspects of the faith, she none the less was recognized as an authority. In fact, due to her not going to any formal school, her nephew, the 4th Imam commonly referred to her as the âThe Scholar who had no formal teacher.â A point which the sisters of today can learn from this towering personality, while in Kufah during the reign of her father, the Commander of the Faithful, she held special sessions for the Muslim women who would come to learn about Islam and a detailed expose' of the Qurâan. Thus, rather than the men teaching the women, she took it upon her self to teach those of her gender not about theology but also Islamic morals and ethics! Her lofty rank and status would however, not grant her immunity from the clutches of tyranny. Although the events surrounding her death are obscure, and there are definitely discrepancies as to what occurred after the massacre in Kerbala in 61 AH to this noble woman, however most historians write that she lived only one year after the massacre and at the age of 57, left this mortal world. Even the reports of where she was buried conflict with one another with three prominent opinions being put forward by the researchers. Some say that she died and was buried in Madinah; others claim Egypt where there is a large shrine for Sayyida Zainab while the third and most compelling belief is that she died in Damascus. âPeace be upon her the day she was born, the day she died and the day she will be brought back to lifeâ¦â Source http://www.world-federation.org/Secretariat/Articles/Archive/Wafat_SayyidaZainab.htm 15th Rajab 62AH. The death anniversary of Lady Zainab [s.a]:* *_On this occassion of sorrow and grief, I wish to extend my condolences to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w), the Holy Ahlul Bayt (a.s), Imam al-Mahdi (atf) and to all Momineen:*_ The mountain of patience, the champion of Karbala and the saviour of her brother Imam Hussein (a.s)'s message! *The Holy Prophet [s.a.w] asked why Jibra'il wept and he answered:* _âO Prophet of Allah, from early on in life this girl will remain entangled in tribulations and trials in this worldâ_ After bearing all those calamities from Karbala to Damascus to Madina, Bibi Zainab [s.a] had returned altered, her hair white, and her back bent. Although upon her return she had been reunited with her husband, she did not live long after the torturous trials she had to bear. After their release from prison, Bibi Zainab (s.a), along with the rest of the members of Ahlul Bayt (a.s) went to Medinah. Even in Medinah, she continued preaching. Islam spread rapidly. text: Ziyarat Hazrat Abbas Ibn Ali(as) Brief info Brief Life × BRotherhood, Courage, and Loyalty in Abbas bin Ali - By SAYYID MUHAMMAD RIZVI Who was Abbas (peace be upon him), whose birth anniversary is being celebrated this week? To the Muslims, Abbas is known in different ways: as the lion of Ali, the hero of Karbala, the flag-bearer of Hussain, the beloved brother of Zainab, and the loving uncle of Sakina (peace be upon them all). Abbas was the son of Imam Ali, the first Imam and successor of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his progeny). He was the brother of Imam Hussain. Fifty years after the demise of the Prophet Muhammad, his grandson Hussain stood up against Yazid, the tyrant ruler of the time, and refused to pledge allegiance to him. As a result of this protest, Hussain, his family-members, and a small group of his companions were surrounded by Yazidi forces in the desert of Karbala, prevented from water for three days, and, finally, on the Day of Ashura, Hussain with about 100 souls faced an army of 25,000 soldiers. They were given the choice of pledging allegiance to Yazid or face death. In that uneven battle, Hussain chose an honorable death over a disgraceful life under a tyrant like Yazid. It was in that historical event that Abbas was made the commander-in-chief and flag-bearer of Hussaini forces. That battle-field gradually turned into a place of pilgrimage, and today the shrines of both these brothers, with their golden domes, form the skyline of Karbala in Iraq. Brotherhood By his supreme sacrifice, Abbas became a universal soul that transcends time and space. Let us start with concept of brotherhood: Brotherhood can be understood on two different levels, a physical and personal level, and a spiritual and social level. Both aspects are important. However, the brotherhood based on blood relationship should be synchronized with the brotherhood based on spiritual relationship. In case of tension between the two relationships, the spiritual brotherhood will take precedence over the physical brotherhood. ("Verily the believers are brethren [of one another]." 49:10) Imam Zainul Abideen (peace be upon him), the fourth Shia Imam and nephew of Abbas, in his famous the Charter of Rights, writes about the rights of a brother. He says brothers should consider one another as a source of support and protection, and they should be sincere in giving advice and helping one another towards the path of God. He concludes by writing: "â¦Then if he obeys his Lord and properly answers His call [it is good for all]; otherwise, Allah, rather than your brother, should be your choice and the object of your reverence." It is human nature for two brothers to love and support one another. Almighty God tends to leave natural issues to nature and does not talk about it that much, and only points out issues when humans deviate from their nature. On brotherhood, there are two negative examples in the Qur'an: the example of Qabil (Cain) who murdered his brother HÃ£bil (Abel); and the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) who conspired to get rid of him. In the scale of zero to ten, we can put Qabil's relationship at zero, and that of Yusuf's brothers at three â on the positive side, we can surely put the relationship of Abbas to Imam Hussain at ten. The devotion of Abbas to Hussain was not just on the physical level; it was also based on the spiritual level. This is reflected in his statement to Shimr bin Dhil Jawshan. Shimr, one of commanders of the Yazidi forces, was related to Abbas through his mother who was from the Kilabiyya tribe (while Hussain's mother was the daughter of the Prophet). Shimr had come to Karbala with an amaan, assurance of protection or amnesty signed by Iraq's governor, for Abbas and his three full brothers. When Shimr presented that amnesty to Abbas, Abbas responded by saying: "May God curse you and your amnesty. You give assurance of protection to us, but the son of the Prophet's daughter has no amnesty!" Abbas bin Ali's message to us is quite clear: we have to strengthen the ties of brotherhood with fellow Muslims irrespective of their race, color, language, or geographical location. All of us are brethren in faith; all other relationships must be synchronized with that. We should be able to feel the pain of one another, as the Prophet Muhammad once said, "Muslims are like one body: when one limb is injured, the hurt is felt by the entire body." Between Abbas and Imam Hussain, this level of closeness and concern is symbolized in the words of Hussain: when he heard Abbas calling for help as he was falling down from the horse, the Imam felt the pain and said, "Now my back has broken, and my options are few." Courage What is courage? In Islamic ethics, courage is not defined by physical strength; courage means to have control over one's emotions and feelings and to use them only for the right cause. A person who only relies on his physical strength and cannot control his emotions is not a courageous person; he is rather a foolhardy person. While describing the Prophet and his true followers, Allah says: "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, and those who are with him are firm against the enemies but soft with their own." (48:29) Iqbal, the famous poet of the Indian sub-continent, presents the same concept in his poetic style: In the struggle of truth, the believer is as solid as the steel But in midst of his friends, he is as soft as the silk Abbas was not the slave of his desires and emotions; even his courage was linked to the spiritual relationship: Abbas was very stern and firm when he confronted the enemies, but he was very kind, compassionate, and caring towards the good people. The children of Hussain and the clan of Banu Hashim adored him. He was the favorite uncle of Sakina, the four years old daughter of Imam Hussain. Unfortunately, what we see in the world today is that the tyrants, the kings, and the generals who rule over Muslim countries behave in the opposite manner: they are humble in front of the enemies but very bold when they deal with their own people and oppress them! When Imam Hussain asked Abbas to try and get water for the children, Abbas confronted the enemy force and he was easily able to disperse them and got access to the river. Abbas entered the river and filled the water-bag with water. On the way back, he had to pass through some palms trees, and that is where the enemy was hiding behind the trees to attack him from the back. One Yazidi soldier attacked him from behind in such a way that he lost his right hand. Abbas courageously got hold of the water-bag and consoled himself by the following verses: By God, though you have severed my right hand My faith, I will surely forever defend I will defend the truthful leader of conviction The grandson of the pure and truthful Prophet Loyalty We see that loyalty is a very important quality, especially the loyalty toward one's faith and community. Abbas's loyalty has become proverbial in the literature of Karbala. On the eve of Ashura, when Imam Hussain asked his friends and family members to go away and leave him, since the enemies were after his blood only, the first person to stand up and express his loyalty was Abbas bin Ali. He said, "And why should we abandon you? So that we may live after you! May God not show us such a day ever." On the day of Ashura, when Imam Hussain asked him to get water for the children, he succeeded in gaining access to the stream. He galloped into the stream, got down, and filled the water-bag. As a person who had been thirsty for three days, Abbas could have quenched his thirst, but he did not do so. Legally as well as morally, nothing prevented him from drinking water. But he did not do so. It was his sense of loyalty to Imam Hussain and the love for Hussain's children that prevented Abbas from drinking the water. While filling the water, he recited the following verses: While Hussain is drinking the syrup of death You are imbibing the coolness of joy When you look at the flag of Abbas, you always see that a water-bag is attached to it, hanging on to it. It reminds us of the loyalty of Abbas to Hussain and his children. That flag challenges us to be loyal and true to our faith and its values. It urges the followers of Abbas to stand up against oppression, tyranny, and injustice in whatever shape or form that we see in our own times â all in the name of God and to serve the cause of God. And so we end with a tribute to Abbas in the famous words of the Sixth Imam who praised him by saying: "I bear witness that you submitted [to your Imam], affirmed [his truth], and were loyal and sincere [to him]." × . Umm-ul-Momineen and the first and most beloved wife of Prophet Mohammad (saw) and mother of Syeda fatima Zahra (sa) 10th of Ramadhan - Death Anniversary of Lady Khadija(a.s.) - Umm-ul-Momineen and the first and most beloved wife of Prophet Mohammad (saw). 7 Reasons Why She Was The Best? Birth and Geneology Bibi Khadija(a.s.) was the first wife of the Holy Prophet(pbuh&hf). She was born in Makka. Her father's name was Khuwaylid bin Asad and he was a wealthy trader. The Geneology of both Prophet Mohammad(pbuh&hf) and Bibi Khadija(a.s.) was the same reaching upto Qusayy. Early Life Her mother and father both died within 10 years of each other. Their wealth was divided amongst the children but it was bibi khadija(a.s.) who took over the family business and expanded it. With the profit she made she helped the poor, widows, orphans, sick and the disabled people of Makka. She had a cousin called Waraqa bin Naufal who was very learned man and who was not an idol worshipper. Both Waraqa and Bibi Khadija were monothiests and believed in one Allah. First contact with Prophet Mohammad(pbuh) Because of her excellent Akhlaq the Arabs (who at that time used to look down upon women) called her Tahira - the pure one. She was also known as the 'Princess of Makkah' because of her wealth. A lot of Arab nobles and princess wanted to marry her but she refused all of them. In 595 AD, Bibi Khadija was looking for someone to be in charge of her caravan to Syria. Hazrat Abu Talib(a.s.) suggested the Prophet Mohammad(pbuh&hf) to her. She had heard of his trustworthiness and agreed to employ him although he did not have much trading experience. To help him she sent her slave Maysara. The trading caravan was a great success and when Bibi Khadija(a.s.) heard of the Prophet's skills and excellent conduct, she became his admirer. Marriage with Prophet Mohammad(pbuh) Soon it was arranged for Bibi Khadija(a.s.) to be married to the Prophet Mohammad(pbuh&hf). At that time, Prophet Mohammad(pbuh&hf) was aged 25 and Bibi Khadiji(a.s.) was 40 years of age. According to Shiite tradition, this was her first marriage and that she was not a widow as is narrated by non-shiite sources. Hazrat Abu Talib(a.s.) read the Nikah on behalf of the Prophet whilst Waqara bin Noufal read it for Bibi Khadija. Hazrat Abu Talib(a.s.) paid the mehr for his nephew and fed the people of Makka for 3 days in celebration. Bibi Khadija too fed the people. The marriage was a very happy one and their first child was a son called Qasim. The second was Abdullah. Both died in infancy. Their third and last child was Bibi Fatema Zahra(s.a.). Her services for Islam When the Prophet used to go to meditate in the cave of Hira on Jabel-e-Noor, it was Bibi Khadija(a.s.) herself who would climb up there to give him his food and necessaries. She was the first person to accept Islam as taught by the Prophet(pbuh&hf). In 616 AD, the Quraish isolated the Bani Hashim (the family of the Prophet) and they took refuge in a ravine called Shib-e-Abu Talib. Bibi Khadija(a.s.) was there too and it was her wealth (which she donated for Islam) that sustained the Muslims at that time. The siege lasted for 3 years during which time they experienced hunger, thirst, and the cold and heat of the desert. Her Death Bibi Khadija(a.s.) was married to the Holy Prophet(pbuh&hf) for 25 years. Shed died in 619 AD on the 10th of Rmazan 3 years before the Hijrah. When she died nothing was left of her wealth - all of it was served for the propagation of Islam. She was buried in Makkah in a cloak of the Holy Prophet(pbuh&hf). Hazrat Abu Talib(a.s.) died in this year too. The Prophet(pbuh&hf) called the year Aam-ul-Huzn (the year of grief). While Bibi Khadija(a.s.) lived, the Holy Prophet(pbuh&hf) did not marry another woman and in later years he always said that she was the best of his wives. He also said that she was one of the four perfect women who had ever lived. The other three are Bibi Aasiya, the wife of Firaun, Bibi Maryam, the mother of Prophet Isa(a.s.), and Bibi Fatima Zahra(s.a.). 10th of Ramadhan - Death Anniversary of Lady Khadija(a.s.) - Umm-ul-Momineen and the first and most beloved wife of Prophet Mohammad (saw).
